item.title: TUM: legacy portal harvested central-login passwords, an admin's credentials reached TUMonline; MFA accounts held
item.description: The Technical University of Munich said on 2026-11-06 that unknown attackers attacked its myTUM portal and captured the central-login passwords of all persons who had signed in there, among them the credentials of a TUMonline system administrator, with which they attacked the campus-management system TUMonline, which TUM took off the network. TUM says accounts with multi-factor authentication were protected, reported the incident to the Bavarian data-protection commissioner and filed a criminal complaint; heise reports that the entry point was a legacy system and that about 60,000 users are concerned.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOA2

Technical University of Munich: attackers captured the central-login passwords of everyone who signed in to the legacy myTUM portal, took a TUMonline system administrator's credentials and attacked the campus-management system; accounts with MFA were protected

The Technical University of Munich says unknown persons attacked its myTUM portal and captured the passwords for the central login to TUM systems, among them login.tum.de and TUMonline, from all persons who had logged in to myTUM; among them were the access credentials of a system administrator for TUMonline, with which the attackers attacked the central campus-management system TUMonline, which TUM then took off the network (translated from German) (TUM, 2026-11-06). TUM says the attackers may have reached the account password, name, private address and date of birth of everyone affected, plus staff and student details, that the attackers' accesses within TUMonline were largely logged and that it currently assumes no further TUMonline data such as grades is affected, and that accounts with multi-factor authentication were protected in this attack (translated from German) (TUM, 2026-11-06). heise, quoting a TUM spokesperson, reports that the attackers entered through a legacy system and that whether data was exfiltrated is still being investigated, and adds that about 60,000 students and employees are concerned (translated from German) (heise online, 2026-11-06). Neither source states how the passwords were captured at myTUM.

Exposure
A public university or other public body that keeps a retired or secondary sign-in portal validating against its central directory, so that every password typed there is a credential for the primary identity and administration systems; TUM's accounts with MFA held, and the lesson transfers to Swiss cantonal and university portals.
Defender takeaway
Inventory legacy and secondary portals that accept the central directory password and retire them or put them behind MFA, require MFA on administrator accounts of campus and school-management systems, and check whether an administrator ever signed in to such a portal.

item.title: Aargau's information-security law and ordinance take effect 1 January 2027; a specialist unit is to get directive powers
item.description: The Aargau government council announced on 2026-11-06 that it adopted the information-security ordinance (InfoSiV) and that the information-security law (InfoSiG) and the ordinance enter into force on 1 January 2027. An information-security specialist unit is to advise cantonal bodies with directive and enforcement powers, and a cantonal cyber coordination office, headed from that date by Bernhard Droz, and a personnel-security-vetting unit sit at the cantonal police.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOA2

Canton Aargau adopts its information-security ordinance (InfoSiV) and sets 1 January 2027 for the information-security law and ordinance, with a specialist unit to receive directive and enforcement powers and a cyber coordination office at the cantonal police

The Aargau government council adopted the information-security ordinance (InfoSiV) and decided that the information-security legislation, the law (InfoSiG) and the ordinance, enters into force on 1 January 2027 (translated from German) (Kanton Aargau, 2026-11-06). The canton says the law anchors uniform standards and a holistic information-security system in the cantonal administration, that an information-security specialist unit is to advise the cantonal bodies and be equipped with directive and enforcement powers so that one detection and defence strategy can be implemented, and that a further specialist unit for personnel security vetting and a cantonal cyber coordination office are being set up, both at the cantonal police (translated from German) (Kanton Aargau, 2026-11-06). The government elected Bernhard Droz, currently head of IT forensics and cybercrime at the cantonal police, as head of the cyber coordination office from 1 January 2027 (translated from German) (Kanton Aargau, 2026-11-06).

The communiqué says nothing about communes or other bearers of public tasks. In February 2025 Netzwoche reported that a majority in the consultation approved bringing them into the law's scope and that entry into force was then planned for 1 July 2026, so the final text decides whether communal bodies are bound (Netzwoche, 2025-02-24).

Exposure
Aargau cantonal bodies from 1 January 2027; whether communes and other bearers of public tasks fall in scope is not stated in the communiqué.
Defender takeaway
From 1 January 2027 Aargau cantonal bodies answer to one information-security specialist unit that is to be equipped to issue binding directives, so the 2026 task is reading the ordinance and the directives the specialist unit issues; the canton describes the unit's planned powers and not detailed duties, and communal IT owners should read the final text to see whether they are covered.

item.title: BOSSAI AI agents took emergency-services data through open ports, public APIs and default credentials
item.description: Acronis TRU describes BOSSAI, an agentic campaign it attributes with high confidence to one operator in Taiwan: a mesh of 12 AI agents, nine active, that over 12 observed days targeted government emergency services, banks, universities and military systems in 11 countries, with confirmed data exfiltration or system access at roughly ten targets in three countries. The confirmed emergency-services harm was patient-care records of a Taipei fire department and dispatch case records of a city 119 system; TRU says the agents failed where authentication was enforced and endpoints were filtered.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB3

Acronis TRU on BOSSAI: one operator's mesh of 12 AI agents took patient-care records and dispatch case data from Taiwanese emergency services through a legacy open port, a public API and default root credentials, and failed wherever authentication was enforced

Acronis TRU found an open attack workstation holding more than 90,000 files and describes BOSSAI as a mesh of 12 AI agents, nine active, driven by a changing roster of language models, with the operator acting as the bridge between agents and typing commands in Traditional Chinese (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04). The agents that executed attacks ran almost exclusively on abliterated open-weight models run locally, after commercial models repeatedly refused offensive requests (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04). In the 12 days TRU observed, the operator targeted government emergency services, banks and lenders, universities and military systems in 11 countries, with confirmed exfiltration or system access at roughly ten targets in three countries and about fifteen more attacked without confirmed compromise (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04).

The confirmed emergency-services harm is the part that matters here. A Taipei fire-department patient-care records platform exposed ECG readings, ambulance video and vital signs from 2018, accessible without credentials; a city's 119 dispatch system yielded case records with incident times, response types, status fields and street-level locations across seven districts from the system's API; and a fire-dispatch vendor's database administration panel opened with default root credentials, exposing 18 or more tables (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04). In an emergency-management system the agents found a hardcoded AES-256 key in front-end JavaScript that exposed session-cookie contents, an administrator identity among them, and a partial server-side request forgery path, without confirming a full compromise (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04). A brute-force run against a national fire agency's single sign-on portal gave no confirmed access, and the critical Apache flaw that the operator's vulnerability platform reported at a disaster-response centre was fabricated, because the port was filtered (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04). TRU says the agents failed where authentication was enforced, where paywalls required valid sessions and where endpoints were properly filtered, and that obscurity no longer protects a system from agents that investigate hundreds of targets at once (Acronis TRU, 2026-11-04).

Exposure
Emergency-service, dispatch and public-safety systems that expose a record API or a legacy data port without authentication, leave default administrator credentials on a vendor's database panel, or ship secrets in front-end JavaScript; those are the weaknesses the agents turned into data, and TRU reports the patient-care and dispatch records as the gravest confirmed harm.
Detection
TRU names sqlmap, nmap and nikto among the most-used tools, so the traffic is ordinary scanner traffic in web access and authentication logs (an inference from the tool list): bursts of SQL-injection probing, repeated sign-in attempts against a single sign-on portal from one source, and logins to a database administration panel with a default account.
Defender takeaway
Swiss dispatch, patient-care and records systems of emergency services are the same target class, so check them for unauthenticated APIs and legacy ports, default root or administrator credentials on vendor panels, and keys or tokens in front-end code; the agents failed wherever authentication was enforced, so closing those gaps is what stops this tooling.

item.title: Brotli flaw hits Desigo CC, Industrial Edge and Mitel; Cisco lists Duo; Mitel and Common Configurator fixes pending
item.description: Between 2026-10-27 and 2026-11-06 Siemens, Mitel and Cisco listed affected products in advisories that cover the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497: Siemens names Desigo CC V8 and V9 (remedy: the latest .NET security updates) and Industrial Edge, where Common Configurator has no fix; Mitel names MiVoice Business and five OpenScape products with updates planned and workaround articles for three; Cisco's combined advisory lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2) and RoomOS among its products with fixes, a longer list of which is dated up to 2027, without saying which of its CVEs each fix addresses. Cisco says it is not aware of malicious use against any Cisco product, and CISA lists the flaw as exploited.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-111497exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder flaw in Siemens Desigo CC and Industrial Edge, Mitel MiVoice Business and OpenScape, with Cisco listing Duo Network Gateway and RoomOS in its combined advisory: Desigo CC takes the .NET updates, while Mitel updates and the Industrial Edge Common Configurator fix are still pending

The Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write caused by improper handling of malformed compressed data (Mitel, 2026-10-28), and CISA lists it as exploited (CISA, 2026-10-27). Siemens' advisory SSA-045512, revised on 2026-11-06, lists Desigo CC V8 and V9, all versions, remedied by installing the latest .NET security updates via Windows Update, and scores the flaw CVSS 3.1 9.8 (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-30). Its Industrial Edge advisory SSA-443410 says an Industrial Edge Management setup with no Management Applications installed needs no action because the affected functionality is not used or exposed, gives fixed versions for six configurator and monitoring applications, and for Common Configurator, which has no fix, says to uninstall all Management Applications and protect the instance with a firewall or WAF, or on a device to stop the application, until a fix is available (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-30).

Mitel's MISA-2026-0010, revision 5.0 of 2026-11-04, rates the flaw high (CVSS 3.1 8.1) and lists MiVoice Business 10.6.0.7 and earlier, its Solution Virtual Instance up to the build in Mitel's table, OpenScape SBC V11R3.4.4 and earlier, OpenScape SESAP V2 R1.1.9 and earlier, OpenScape Contact Center V12R0 to V12R0FR7, OpenScape Xpert V9 R0.2.0 and earlier and OpenScape Endpoint Management V1 R2.5.1 and earlier as affected; for each an update is planned, not released, and workaround articles exist for OpenScape SBC, SESAP and Contact Center (Mitel, 2026-10-28). Mitel rates the risk low for MiVoice Business, Xpert and Endpoint Management when deployed according to its guidelines, and still lists several products as under investigation (Mitel, 2026-10-28).

Cisco's advisory, version 1.8 of 2026-11-06 and revised often, says its PSIRT is aware that proof-of-concept exploit code is available and is not aware of any malicious use against any Cisco product; it lists Catalyst SD-WAN, IOS XE, IOS XR and Secure Firewall ASA, FMC and FTD as not impacted and Identity Services Engine as under investigation (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27). Its one fix table for the advisory's four CVEs, with no column for which CVE a fix addresses, lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2), Spaces (24.22.1), RoomOS on Board, Desk and Room Series devices (on-premises 11.41.2.3 and 26.7.4.3) and a longer list whose fixes are dated November 2026 to July 2027 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
A Desigo CC host, an Industrial Edge Management instance with Management Applications installed or a Common Configurator on an Edge device, a Mitel MiVoice Business or OpenScape system at the listed versions, or a Cisco Duo Network Gateway or RoomOS device that Cisco lists in its combined advisory, below the builds above. Mitel says the impact on its products may differ from its rating because of product architecture (Mitel, 2026-10-28), so the vendor tables are the check.
Defender takeaway
Install the current .NET updates on every Desigo CC host. On Industrial Edge, update the monitoring and configurator applications to the fixed versions and, where Common Configurator runs, uninstall all Management Applications or stop it on Edge devices until Siemens ships a fix. Apply Mitel's workaround articles for OpenScape SBC, SESAP and Contact Center while no update is released, update Duo Network Gateway to the 3.4.2 that Cisco's table lists, and re-read Cisco's advisory, revised often, before relying on a fix date; Cisco says it is not aware of malicious use against its products, while CISA lists the flaw as exploited.

item.title: Update: Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs ARTEX at machine speed; Mandiant now sees agent frameworks in incident-response cases
item.description: Microsoft reports that Storm-3358, a Cambodia-based, financially motivated cluster, has used ARTEX since October 2026 against financial organisations, pairing it with conventional scanners and installing the open-source remote access tools WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2; Check Point Research reads ten exposed operator consoles showing campaigns that run almost autonomously once a goal is set, and Microsoft says honeypots, decoys, tarpits and fake wins helped reduce the attack traffic reaching real assets.
item.content:encoded:
Update07 Nov 2026 03:50 UTCrun 2026-11-07T0256Z-intelsummaryentitiestechniquessourcesevidencesourcing_note

Microsoft reports that Storm-3358, a Cambodia-based, financially motivated cluster, has used ARTEX since October 2026 against financial organisations, pairing it with conventional scanners and installing the open-source remote access tools WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2; Check Point Research reads ten exposed operator consoles showing campaigns that run almost autonomously once a goal is set, and Microsoft says honeypots, decoys, tarpits and fake wins helped reduce the attack traffic reaching real assets.

Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports that Storm-3358, a Cambodia-based intrusion cluster that primarily targets financial organisations in Southeast Asia and a smaller number of large financial organisations globally, began using ARTEX against the financial sector in October 2026 (Microsoft, 2026-11-06). Microsoft says the cluster combines ARTEX with conventional automated tools to scan internet-facing systems, exploit flaws including anonymous file upload and server-side request forgery, and install the open-source remote access tools WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2, which ARTEX agents download with netcat and curl (Microsoft, 2026-11-06). Microsoft's tell for an agent on a scanned system is "a wide variety of requests in a brief time", retries of variations on one technique and a move to next-stage actions at machine speed; ARTEX by default drives Nmap, curl, wget, Python HTTP clients and headless Chromium through Playwright, and blocking their default traits will not stop an agent, which "will quickly change them" (Microsoft, 2026-11-06). In Microsoft's testing, honeypots, decoys, tarpits and fake wins helped reduce the attack traffic reaching real assets, with no figures given (Microsoft, 2026-11-06).

Check Point Research counts 2,557 systems that host or hosted ARTEX panels, 1,608 of them live and public, and ten that exposed the full database; in those ten consoles the operators set a goal and then "barely interacted with their agent fleets" (Check Point, 2026-11-05). The campaigns it reads are opportunistic crime, not espionage: iOS signing certificates from grey-market shops, a cryptocurrency-service campaign and game-account credentials. In the signing-shop campaign the agents got in through hardcoded administrator passwords in JavaScript bundles, missing API authentication, command injection, insecure direct object references, weak administrative credentials and template injection (Check Point, 2026-11-05). Check Point does not name Storm-3358.

Open finding: ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration →

item.title: Update: Cisco's mail gateway can be rooted by one crafted email; found in a TAC support case, exploitation confirmed
item.description: Rapid7's Metasploit framework now carries public modules for two unauthenticated SQL injections on Cisco Secure Email Gateway that end in root command execution: one merged on 2026-11-05 for the injection its author matches, at medium confidence, to the exploited CVE-2026-76461 and which needs URL Filtering and URL Retrospective Service enabled, and one for the non-default S/MIME public-key harvesting feature that Rapid7 believes is CVE-2026-76443. A clean mail_logs check does not rule out the S/MIME injection, and Cisco's hardening advisory names no fixed 16.0 build.
item.content:encoded:
Update07 Nov 2026 03:49 UTCrun 2026-11-07T0256Z-intelsummarycvesactionssourcesevidencesourcing_notebodytagsimmediate_action

Rapid7's Metasploit framework now carries public modules for two unauthenticated SQL injections on Cisco Secure Email Gateway that end in root command execution: one merged on 2026-11-05 for the injection its author matches, at medium confidence, to the exploited CVE-2026-76461 and which needs URL Filtering and URL Retrospective Service enabled, and one for the non-default S/MIME public-key harvesting feature that Rapid7 believes is CVE-2026-76443. A clean mail_logs check does not rule out the S/MIME injection, and Cisco's hardening advisory names no fixed 16.0 build.

Rapid7's Metasploit framework now carries public exploit modules for two unauthenticated SQL injections on Cisco Secure Email Gateway that end in command execution as root. The first, merged on 2026-11-05, targets an injection in the Email Cloud Scanner URL-retrospective message database and its documentation says "URL Filtering and URL Retrospective Service must both be enabled" (Rapid7 Metasploit module documentation, 2026-10-16), which sits against Cisco's statement that the flaw affects the gateway "regardless of device configuration" (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-09-14); its author says it can only be assessed with medium confidence that this is CVE-2026-76461, the flaw CISA lists, and that of the injections reproduced from the patch diff it was the only one that left the pattern COPY.*TO PROGRAM in mail_logs, the check Cisco's own advisory names (Rapid7 Metasploit pull request 22024, 2026-10-16). The second targets an injection in the S/MIME public-key harvesting feature, "we have reason to believe this maps to CVE-2026-76443" according to Rapid7's wrap-up of 2026-11-06 (Rapid7, 2026-11-06). The S/MIME module was merged on 2026-10-28; its author tested a gateway on AsyncOS 15.5.1-055 with the S/MIME Public Key Harvesting feature enabled for inbound mail, and the module sends one signed S/MIME email carrying 500 certificate addresses to the gateway's SMTP listener (Rapid7 Metasploit pull request 22018, 2026-10-15). Its documentation says "Public-key harvesting must be enabled on the inbound mail flow policy for the target to be exploitable" (Rapid7 Metasploit module documentation, 2026-10-15), and the author of the first module calls that feature "a different non-default feature" (Rapid7 Metasploit pull request 22024, 2026-10-16).

Cisco's hardening advisory lists CVE-2026-76443 with the other grouped CVEs and its fixed-release table gives 15.5.5-014 for 15.5 and earlier, 16.5.0-780 for 16.5 and "Migrate to a fixed release." for 16.0 (Cisco PSIRT, hardening-release advisory, 2026-09-14). A 16.0 appliance on 16.0.4-302 therefore has no named fix for the flaw the S/MIME module most likely uses; moving to 16.5.0-780 closes it. Rapid7 does not report exploitation of the S/MIME module's flaw, and Cisco does not say whether the injection it lists as exploited is the one in either module.

Open finding: CVE-2026-76461: Cisco Secure Email Gateway unauthenticated SQL injection in email parsing reaches root command execution, exploited before disclosure (CVSS 9.8) →

item.title: Entra app-credential abuse: agents hunt GitHub for secrets, an operator reaches MSP clients, government among them
item.description: Microsoft reports that since August threat actors have used the agentic framework ARTEX to query public GitHub for OAuth application secrets and cloud keys, and that from 2026-10-28 valid application credentials were used for service-principal sign-ins across dozens of applications in several tenants, a vendor-owned multitenant application among them. Todyl's telemetry shows one operator since 2026-11-01 targeting about 45 application registrations at MSPs, more than 33 of which authenticated, and reaching 27 organisations, government clients among them; Microsoft says a similar campaign involving the same addresses was reported by Todyl, while Todyl does not tie its case to ARTEX and cannot say where the secrets came from.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHNATOB2

Exposed application credentials: Microsoft sees an agentic framework search GitHub for OAuth and cloud application secrets and then sign in as the applications from 2026-10-28, and Todyl sees an operator use MSP applications to reach 27 organisations, government clients among them

Microsoft reports that since August 2026 threat actors have used the agentic offensive framework ARTEX to submit large volumes of queries to public GitHub for secrets (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05). As early as 2026-10-28 it saw successful service-principal sign-ins from two IP addresses, one a Tor exit node that may carry unrelated activity, across dozens of applications in several tenants, including a vendor-owned multitenant application whose credential was compromised at the source and used to reach multiple downstream tenants (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05). Microsoft states that a similar campaign involving the same addresses was also reported by Todyl (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05).

Todyl, from its managed-detection telemetry, describes one operator who since 2026-11-01 has signed in to MSPs' Microsoft 365 and Azure environments as their own applications with stolen credentials that are still valid: about 45 app registrations at roughly 18 organisations were targeted, more than 33 authenticated, and 27 organisations were reached, among them the MSPs' downstream clients in government (Todyl, 2026-11-03). For nearly every credential the operator requests an Azure Resource Manager token, then a Key Vault token, and within minutes applications that had never been used start authenticating; MSP multitenant and delegated-admin apps and Partner Center tokens reach client tenants, one app sweeping 15 client tenants in about 10-second loops (Todyl, 2026-11-03). Todyl says no Microsoft vulnerability is involved, that it saw no persistence and does not know how the credentials were obtained, and that several seed secrets had only ever been used from staff devices and office networks, which points to a file store or live backend rather than configurations crawled from the internet (Todyl, 2026-11-03). After its detections fired on 2026-11-03 the operator switched to spoofed browser user agents and replayed users' refresh tokens, all blocked by Conditional Access (Todyl, 2026-11-03).

Exposure
Any Entra tenant, an MSP's or a customer's, that holds app registrations with client secrets, above all multitenant, delegated-admin and Partner Center applications and Azure DevOps service connections, security-tool integration apps among those abused (Todyl, 2026-11-03); Conditional Access for workload identities needs the Workload ID Premium licence and covers only single-tenant apps (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05).
Detection
In Entra service-principal and non-interactive sign-in logs, an invalid-secret or expired-secret error for an application followed by a success, one address authenticating as service principals in several unrelated tenants within 24 hours, an Azure Resource Manager token followed at once by a Key Vault token and then by previously unused apps authenticating, and failed service-principal sign-ins from hosting space that never succeed, which success-only logic misses (Todyl, 2026-11-03). In Azure DevOps auditing, personal access token creation and first use, federated service connections and pipeline edits (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05).

Triage: the invalid-secret and expired-secret errors alone only show that someone holds an old or wrong credential for the app; Microsoft treats a failure followed by a success as the urgent case (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05).

Defender takeaway
Inventory the client secrets on app registrations and hunt the sign-in pattern above in every tenant you run or manage, MSP-managed communal tenants included; on an affected app remove every client secret, certificate and federated credential, including those the actor added, and rotate what any Key Vault it could read holds, because tokens already issued stay valid until expiry (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-05).

item.title: Update: Zyxel GS1900: Binarly says the exploit GreyNoise caught works on the June-fixed builds; install the .3C0 builds
item.description: Binarly shows the exploit GreyNoise described works against all ten June-fixed GS1900 builds because it targets a separate flaw, CVE-2026-107441, which Zyxel fixed in the .3C0 builds on 2026-10-22 and disclosed on 2026-11-03; the .3C0 builds replace the .2C0 builds as the remedy, and exploitation of the new CVE rests on Binarly's exploit match, which neither Zyxel nor CISA confirms.
item.content:encoded:
Update05 Nov 2026 03:59 UTCrun 2026-11-05T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarycvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodyclassification

Binarly shows the exploit GreyNoise described works against all ten June-fixed GS1900 builds because it targets a separate flaw, CVE-2026-107441, which Zyxel fixed in the .3C0 builds on 2026-10-22 and disclosed on 2026-11-03; the .3C0 builds replace the .2C0 builds as the remedy, and exploitation of the new CVE rests on Binarly's exploit match, which neither Zyxel nor CISA confirms.

Binarly reports that the Python exploit GreyNoise described, which it found in an exposed archive on infrastructure that BleepingComputer ties to Red Heron (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-04), targets a flaw in the request-parameter parser of the switches' CGI (dispatcher.cgi), not the stack overflow of CVE-2026-7273, and that it works without change against the "…(x).2C0" builds Zyxel advertised as the June fix; Binarly confirmed this against all ten builds on 2026-09-28 (Binarly, 2026-11-03). Zyxel treats the report as a separate vulnerability, CVE-2026-107441, fixed on 2026-10-22 in the "…(x).3C0" builds of GS1900-8, -8HP, -10HP, -16, -24, -24E, -24EP, -24HPv2, -48 and -48HPv2 and disclosed in an advisory of 2026-11-03 that credits Binarly and shows no score or exploitation statement (Zyxel PSIRT, 2026-11-03; Binarly, 2026-11-03). Binarly labels the flaw an in-the-wild zero-day on the strength of the exploit match, scores it 9.8 with a network vector against Zyxel's LAN-based wording, and says it will publish a minimised proof of concept; CISA's catalog of 2026-11-04 lists only CVE-2026-7273 (Binarly, 2026-11-03; Binarly, 2026-11-03; BleepingComputer, 2026-11-04; CISA KEV, 2026-11-04). Switches on the June build are therefore still exposed to the exploit until the "…(x).3C0" build is installed.

Open finding: CVE-2026-7273 and CVE-2026-107441, Zyxel GS1900 switches: GreyNoise caught a Red Heron-linked actor exfiltrating configurations and hashed root credentials from 996 switches in 48 countries, and Binarly shows its exploit targets a separate flaw that the June fix leaves open; only the .3C0 builds close it →

item.title: Bitdefender: a 3AM affiliate joined a school estate's AD domains with new trusts after stealing Veeam credentials
item.description: Bitdefender MDR describes a September 2026 intrusion by a 3AM ransomware affiliate into a UK school estate that began as several unconnected Active Directory domains: a modified public Veeam script decrypted credentials stored on three backup servers, the attacker created two backdoor domain-administrator accounts, joined three domains with new two-way trusts within about three hours, tried to remove EDR agents (anti-tampering blocked it) and encrypted machines. Initial access is unknown, every attacker action Bitdefender saw came from an unmanaged internal host, and Bitdefender reads the 40 to 101 second retry cadence as a model-driven loop, flagged as its own interpretation; it says a new trust between domains is a rare change that is cheap to alert on.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

3AM ransomware affiliate in a UK school estate: Bitdefender documents backup-credential theft, rogue domain admins and new two-way trusts between Active Directory domains, with a command-retry pattern it reads as a model-driven loop

Bitdefender MDR attributes the intrusion to a 3AM (ThreeAM) ransomware affiliate on the encryptor build and its command-line pattern; the target was a school estate in the UK whose domains began as separate Active Directory environments, and initial access is unknown (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03). In September 2026 the attacker first took credentials from the backup software: a modified copy of a public script read the credentials stored in Veeam's databases on three backup servers and decrypted them with the Windows Data Protection API, and a browser credential database was copied from a terminal server (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03). It then worked with built-in tools (PowerShell, WMI, reg, netsh, rundll32) and a few public ones (an Impacket-like remote-execution tool that returns output over administrative shares, Mimikatz renamed to look like a monitoring binary), enumerated domain trusts from a domain controller, searched SYSVOL logon scripts for the names and subnets of other schools, created two backdoor domain-administrator accounts, joined three separate domains with two-way trusts within about three hours, tried to remove EDR agents, which anti-tampering controls blocked, deleted system-state backups and encrypted machines with a Rust-based encryptor (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

Bitdefender's reading, which it calls interpretation and not a finding, is that a model drove part of the work: commands call the Veeam web interface on a port and with a login method that do not match the vendor documentation, output is self-labelled, scripts carry numbered revisions, and retries arrive 40 to 101 seconds apart whatever the size of the change, while a new task takes minutes. Every attacker action Bitdefender saw came from an unmanaged internal host with no agent, so the automation itself was never seen, and Bitdefender says it could not document anything about a language model (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

Exposure
A Windows estate that runs Veeam Backup & Replication and has several Active Directory domains or a flat network that an unmanaged internal host can reach; the unmanaged host is the gap, because it ran no agent and sat outside Bitdefender's visibility.
Detection
In directory-service change events, new trust relationships between domains, which Bitdefender calls a rare change that is cheap to alert on, and new domain-administrator group members; in backup-server logs, Veeam web-interface calls and credential-store reads from hosts that are not backup administrators'; in endpoint telemetry, saves of the SECURITY, SYSTEM or SAM registry hives by any process that is not a known backup or administration job, LSASS access, a Windows Defender exclusion for the temporary directory, and the same command re-issued with small edits at a steady cadence; across hosts, file contents staged into registry values, which Bitdefender calls an unusual channel and a strong indicator to hunt for, and sent out by HTTP POST to an internal host, and probe or confirmation artifacts such as a scheduled task named for the probe left on production hosts; in authentication logs, unmanaged hosts authenticating to domain controllers (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).
Defender takeaway
Alert on any new domain trust and on additions to the domain-administrator groups, alert on credential-reading access to backup-software databases and on saves of the SECURITY, SYSTEM or SAM hives outside known backup or administration jobs, put an endpoint agent on every machine because the staging host here was unmanaged, and limit remote execution and administrative shares to known management hosts (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

item.title: Update: Berlin confirms extortion after a phishing click reaches the shared state network; media reports name Rhysida
item.description: rbb24 Recherche reported on 2026-10-21 that the Senate department for urban development's attack-detection licences covered only five percent of devices and that neither the entry endpoint nor the servers the data left from were covered; BSI told rbb24 it does not confirm that the Berlin attack followed the TerminalFix pattern.
item.content:encoded:
Update02 Nov 2026 03:47 UTCrun 2026-11-02T0256Z-intelsourcing_notesourcesevidencebodypriorityconfidenceclassification

rbb24 Recherche reported on 2026-10-21 that the Senate department for urban development's attack-detection licences covered only five percent of devices and that neither the entry endpoint nor the servers the data left from were covered; BSI told rbb24 it does not confirm that the Berlin attack followed the TerminalFix pattern.

rbb24 Recherche reported on 2026-10-21 that the attack-detection system introduced in 2026 had licences for only five percent of all devices, according to the Senate department for urban development, which also said that extending it to every device was not possible "for financial reasons"; rbb's research shows that neither the endpoint identified as the criminals' entry point nor the servers from which data later flowed were covered by it (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21). Both departments also said that in 2024 the funds needed for IT security were available only in part to the extent required, although the state's information-security guideline has obliged agencies since 2017 to provide enough staff and money (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21). The stolen data includes a copy of the transport senator's identity card and of her digital signature and, rbb's analysis shows, further identity-card copies and personal documents of employees; the mobility department confirmed to rbb that the data is mostly unstructured files from shared and personal directories (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21).

BSI told rbb that it had warned repeatedly since at least March 2025 of fake security prompts that make users run a malicious command themselves, publicly and in daily situation reports that also went to representatives of the federal states, and that it described the TerminalFix variant in September 2026; it does not confirm to rbb that the Berlin attack followed that pattern, saying only that it is in close contact with Berlin and supporting the response (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21). BSI's advisory of 2026-09-04 does not name Berlin (BSI, BITS-2026-287419-1032, 2026-09-04), so the link between TerminalFix and this incident rests on BSI's Mastodon post, which heise reads as confirmation (heise online, 2026-09-07), and not on a BSI statement to rbb that the Berlin attack followed that pattern. rbb describes the chain for such warnings: the Berlin-CERT run by the IT service centre ITDZ passes relevant reports to each agency's information-security officers, and each agency is itself responsible for acting on them; the ITDZ and the Senate Chancellery did not say whether BSI's warnings reached the two departments or what followed (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21).

Defender takeaway
The transferable gap is licence coverage, not the absence of a tool. Compare the endpoints and servers that actually run the detection agent, file servers holding shared and personal directories first, with the estate, and settle who in a federated administration is accountable for acting on a national-CERT warning, because in Berlin's chain the ITDZ and the Senate Chancellery left open whether the warnings reached the two departments.

Open finding: Berlin's state government confirms an extortion attempt after a phishing click opens the shared Landesnetz; media reporting names Rhysida →

item.title: Android 'SMS of Death': one hidden SMS drops calls, emergency calls included; Android 12 and 13 get no fix
item.description: An independent researcher published a working proof of concept on 2026-10-29 for a zero-click remote denial of service in Android's telephony framework: one malformed WAP Push data message crashes the com.android.phone process, drops active calls including emergency calls and, because the message is retried, can leave a phone in a restart loop. Per the researcher, Google's fix shipped in the October 2026 update for Android 14 to 17, so Android 12 and 13 phones run the same code unfixed; no source reports exploitation.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

Android telephony ('SMS of Death'): one hidden WAP Push message crashes the phone process and drops calls, emergency calls included; fixed for Android 14 to 17 in the October 2026 update according to the researcher, Android 12 and 13 stay exposed, public proof of concept

A researcher who signs as Mark B published a working proof-of-concept app on 2026-10-29 for a zero-click remote denial of service in Android's telephony framework (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29). One malformed WAP Push data message to port 2948 makes WapPushOverSms.decodeWapPdu() cast a 64-bit header length to a signed 32-bit integer and allocate a negative-sized array; the uncaught NegativeArraySizeException kills the com.android.phone process, which drops active calls, emergency calls included, and cuts service for one to two seconds per message (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29). The poison message stays in the pending queue and is retried on every boot and on carrier redelivery: the researcher reports that about 20 messages leave a device unusable and that one Android 12 phone rebooted into recovery roughly every 90 seconds until the messages were deleted over ADB (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29). The crash reproduced on Android 12 to 16, on a Pixel 9 and on Samsung Galaxy and A-series phones (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29); Security Affairs restates the mechanism and the October fix for Android 14 to 17 (Security Affairs, 2026-11-01).

Google's fix, titled "Fix remote DoS in decodeWapPdu", catches the exceptions the malformed messages trigger and deletes the malicious messages from the SMS database (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-31); per the researcher it shipped in the October 2026 update for Android 14 to 17, so Android 12 and 13 phones outside the update window run the same code unfixed (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29). BleepingComputer adds that the fix is not listed in Google's October bulletin (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-31). The proof-of-concept app and its source are public (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29; BleepingComputer, 2026-10-31), and none of the sources reports use in the wild.

Exposure
Any Android phone on a patch level before October 2026, and Android 12 and 13 phones outside the security-update window, which receive no fix; the attack needs only the target's phone number (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29). The patch level in device-management inventory shows which handsets have the fix.
Detection
On managed handsets, repeated crashes of the com.android.phone process in the device log, with a NegativeArraySizeException raised in WapPushOverSms.decodeWapPdu, calls that end with disconnect cause CS_DEATH, and a phone that restarts into recovery about every 90 seconds (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29); the message never appears in the inbox and the sender is not shown, so the crash log is the only trace on the phone.

Triage: a single telephony restart has many benign causes; a restart that recurs on every boot or on each carrier redelivery, with the exception above in the crash log, matches this flaw.

Defender takeaway
Move every managed Android handset to the October 2026 patch level, emergency-service and on-call staff first, and list for replacement the Android 12 and 13 phones outside the security-update window, which receive no fix and stay crashable by one message. A phone stuck in the loop should not be wiped from the recovery prompt: the researcher documents deleting the pending WAP Push rows over ADB from a computer, which avoids a factory reset (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29).

Sources: Mark B (smsofdeath.com) · BleepingComputer · Security Affairs

Update01 Nov 2026 03:29 UTCrun 2026-11-01T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryentitiestechniquessourcesevidencesourcing_note

Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report that since late August they have seen ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN operated inside incident-response cases, with ARTEX adopted by extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters whose victims include US government organizations; they track the Wiz-observed ARTEX campaign as UNC7228, overlapping Storm-0940, and say the original ARTEX repository was taken down in October while forks keep spreading it. The agent's log signature is bursts of roughly 2 to 25 seconds, error-driven retries and, in one case, MySQL general-log changes likely intended to write JSP web shells.

Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant report that since late August 2026 they have seen threat actors operate ARTEX, PentAGI, CAIRN and possibly custom harnesses inside Mandiant incident-response engagements, with agents carrying out significant parts of the attack lifecycle such as lateral movement, database exploitation and exfiltration preparation (GTIG and Mandiant, 2026-10-31). They say ARTEX has been adopted since late August by financially motivated extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters, whose operations affected organizations in government, technology, chemicals and materials, and manufacturing in the United States, and that the campaign Wiz tracks, which GTIG tracks as UNC7228, overlaps with Microsoft's Storm-0940 and dates back to at least August 2026 (GTIG and Mandiant, 2026-10-31). The original ARTEX repository was taken down by its creator in October because of abuse, but community forks, among them a commercial one, keep the framework in circulation (GTIG and Mandiant, 2026-10-31).

In several cases the operators handed ARTEX compromised credentials and told it to run the later stages. GTIG's log signature for the agent is execution in bursts of roughly 2 to 25 seconds, error-driven retries and forensically noisy trial and error; in one case, given valid credentials, the framework used an application's SQL API to point the MySQL general log at a web-accessible .jsp path and then ran SELECT statements carrying script tags, likely intended to write web shells under somewhat-incremental file names until they ran cleanly (GTIG and Mandiant, 2026-10-31).

item.title: Update: BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day: Rapid7 reports a Metasploit module; the actor's persistence survives reset
item.description: Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis of CVE-2026-102764 on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the unauthenticated file-write to code-execution chain; its successful request is an extensionless URL that rules matching only .php requests miss.
item.content:encoded:
Update31 Oct 2026 03:39 UTCrun 2026-10-31T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryimmediate_actionsourcesevidenceactionsbody

Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis of CVE-2026-102764 on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the unauthenticated file-write to code-execution chain; its successful request is an extensionless URL that rules matching only .php requests miss.

Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the chain, with PHP and Unix Command targets (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). An anonymous customer session, started through the public customer connection, sends a message whose source address carries a reserved local router ID; the appliance's customer worker accepts that address as proof that the request came from a local component, which exposes an internal file-transfer service with its native filesystem provider. Rapid7 used it to write a PHP file into the site's public directory and ran it as the site's operating-system user (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). The successful request was an extensionless URL, because the web server answers a direct .php request with 404 and maps an extensionless URL to the existing file, so detection that only searches for requests ending in .php would miss it; the appliance's thin-scc logs record file-transfer stream creation and rejected requests (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). Rapid7 tested Remote Support 24.1.2 and says other affected releases and fixed builds have not been established (Rapid7, 2026-10-30); BeyondTrust's advisory remains the reference for affected and fixed versions (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

Open finding: CVE-2026-102764, BeyondTrust Remote Support: an unauthenticated file-operation flaw exploited as a zero-day since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor that left a web shell and boot-time sudo persistence (CVSS 4.0 9.3) →

item.title: privatim cloud guidance v3.02: public bodies keep their own keys for sensitive data; big-vendor SaaS mostly out
item.description: privatim, the conference of the Swiss data-protection authorities, revised its guidance on cloud-specific risks for public bodies on 2026-10-02 (version 3.02, replacing the version of 3 February 2022). For particularly sensitive personal data the public body must encrypt with keys only it can use, outsourcing such data or data under a statutory duty of confidentiality to SaaS solutions of large international providers is in most cases inadmissible, and the body's top management is to confirm the residual risk in writing.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOA2

privatim revises its cloud guidance for Swiss public bodies (Merkblatt v3.02, 2 October 2026): sensitive data stays under the body's own keys, SaaS from Microsoft, Google, AWS and SAP is in most cases inadmissible for secrecy-bound data, and top management signs the residual risk

privatim, the conference of the Swiss data-protection authorities, dates version 3.02 of its guidance "Cloud-specific risks and measures" to 2 October 2026 (privatim, 2026-10-02); it replaces the version of 3 February 2022 (DCOD, 2026-10-27). For particularly sensitive personal data the public body must encrypt, the keys may be available only to it, and outsourcing such data, or data under a statutory duty of confidentiality, to SaaS from large international providers, with Microsoft, Google, AWS and SAP named, is in most cases inadmissible because of the untenable risk (privatim, 2026-10-02). Keys may stay with the provider only where no untenable risk follows and the provider is bound by contract to use them only with the body's express consent and to log every access (privatim, 2026-10-02).

The body, or its top management, is to confirm in writing that it has understood the risks and accepts the residual risk, and data the cloud services generate about their users, such as telemetry and logging data, is to be treated with the same care and contract terms as the content data (privatim, 2026-10-02). The five risk areas are contract design, places of processing including foreign authority access, confidentiality with encryption and key management, user data, and sub-processors (privatim, 2026-10-02).

Defender takeaway
The guidance addresses public bodies subject to Swiss data-protection law; a body that runs or plans SaaS from the named providers for sensitive or secrecy-bound data is advised to keep its own encryption keys, to have top management sign the residual risk, and to hold provider telemetry and logs about its users to the same contract terms.

item.title: Lumen: Volt Typhoon's Silent Train relay chains fronted zero-days against SD-WAN, N-central and KACE
item.description: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon ran exploitation, credential access and exfiltration through Silent Train, rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices that it rebuilt for each operation, and that its monitoring uncovered one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators, among them Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, N-able N-central and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator. The reported victims are US-centred and the report names no Swiss or European victim.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

Silent Train: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs describes the rotating relay network Volt Typhoon used for one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against management and control-plane platforms (Quest KACE, Versa Director, N-able N-central, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator)

Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon used a covert framework it calls Silent Train, first seen in late 2023, for the phases that need protection: exploitation, credential access, data exfiltration and continued access to victims (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). A session starts from a virtual private server outside the US, passes through compromised non-US SOHO and IoT devices and leaves through a compromised US device before the victim; more than 27 device classes were enrolled, from TP-Link routers and Netgear Orbi devices to Fortinet appliances and CyberPanel servers, and the enterprise platforms stayed in chains for one to three months as final hops (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The operators exploit exposed web interfaces on the relay devices and deploy only what chained SSH needs, namely temporary SSH services, keys, configuration files and living-off-the-land utilities, with reverse tunnels over open-source proxies in later variants; sessions averaged about four hours, and at the end the operators removed all artifacts and dismantled the chain (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28).

Lumen says its monitoring helped identify one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators: Quest KACE, where the activity looked like an undisclosed flaw, affected more than 30 victims and fell after Quest's October 2025 updates (a moderate-confidence assessment); Versa Director in 2024; the N-able N-central flaws CVE-2025-8875 and CVE-2025-8876; Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN through CVE-2026-20127, exploited by late 2025 and after Cisco's February 2026 disclosure; and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator through the zero-day later designated CVE-2026-16812 (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). Post-incident analysis found in-memory webshells, credential harvesting and abuse of native platform features such as endpoint control and remote file transfers, and in several cases erased or altered logs (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The victims it names are US government, telecommunications, defence-industrial, managed-service and critical-infrastructure organisations, concentrated in Hawaii, California and Texas, and it names no European or Swiss victim (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The Hacker News carries the same findings from a report Lumen shared with it (The Hacker News, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
Internet-reachable management and control-plane platforms (endpoint management, SD-WAN controllers and orchestrators, out-of-band administration), and edge devices with exposed web interfaces, which can be enrolled as relay hops without any data of the owner being the target.
Detection
Telemetry classes are administrative logins, API calls, remote file transfers and configuration changes on management platforms outside normal administration hours or workflow, in-memory web shells that leave no file on disk, and, on edge devices, temporary SSH services, unfamiliar keys and outbound reverse tunnels to unfamiliar upstream hosts (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28).
Defender takeaway
Restrict the administrative interfaces of management and control-plane platforms to a VPN, jump host or management network and prioritise their patching, as Lumen advises, and treat an edge device that shows temporary SSH services or reverse tunnels as a possible relay in someone else's intrusion chain.

item.title: CrowdStrike: VAPOR PANDA runs ARTEX against 200+ organisations, European foreign ministries among them
item.description: CrowdStrike reports that from 2026-10-17 the China-nexus actor VAPOR PANDA used the ARTEX agent framework, driven mainly by the DeepSeek model, against more than 200 organisations worldwide, with the controller CrowdStrike saw directing exploitation in at least 14 countries, including foreign ministries in Europe, a European country's presidency, prime minister's office and defence, justice, finance and intelligence entities, and a Greek government entity. CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation at nine organisations, with the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor loaded by a renamed legitimate binary, and says this campaign is separate from the Storm-0940 ARTEX activity Microsoft reported.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB3

VAPOR PANDA: CrowdStrike reports a China-nexus actor running the ARTEX agent framework against more than 200 organisations from 17 October, among them foreign ministries in Europe and a Greek government entity, and deploying the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor

CrowdStrike OverWatch reports that from 2026-10-17 a single ARTEX controller linked to VAPOR PANDA infrastructure directed exploitation against entities in at least 14 countries over 11 days, and that the campaign reached more than 200 organisations, including foreign ministries in Europe (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). One engagement focused on a single European country, its foreign ministry, presidency, prime minister's office and defence, justice, finance and intelligence entities, and another targeted 19 US organisations in pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, defence, nuclear and finance (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation at nine organisations and password spraying and credential scanning against at least 12 more, among them government entities in Europe (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). CrowdStrike states that the campaign is separate from the Storm-0940 ARTEX activity Microsoft reported and is VAPOR PANDA's first observed use of AI-driven tooling (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).

The framework ran mainly on the DeepSeek model, with a human operator steering the agents at decision points while they pursued web, cloud, container, Active Directory, mail and VPN paths in parallel (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). In transcripts at a US pharmaceutical company the agent chained an unsigned SAML assertion with an XML external entity flaw to query the cloud instance metadata service and obtain a role that could issue administration commands to thousands of instances; at a second it deployed web shells, abused an unauthenticated orchestration service for root in a container environment, read LAPS passwords and abused resource-based constrained delegation (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). Against a Greek government entity the operator supplied a 2022 directory export from the mail server whose authentication keys had likely not been rotated; the agent forged an administrator token, read mailboxes and used VPN configurations from a user's sent mail, with a VPN client key the operator described as coming from a May 2024 email leak, to reach the internal network (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). The operator also told the agents to find domain Windows hosts without the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). At a Middle East interior ministry and a Latin American foreign ministry the actor loaded the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor through a legitimate GameHook binary renamed svchost.exe that loads a malicious DLL (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). No Swiss target is named.

Exposure
Government, mail, identity and VPN estates where a directory export or backup holding authentication keys has never been rotated, SAML service providers that accept unsigned assertions, and cloud instances that still allow instance metadata service version 1; CrowdStrike names foreign ministries and government entities in Europe among the targets (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).
Detection
Telemetry classes are authentication logs (password spraying and credential scanning against many accounts, an administrator token minted outside the identity provider, VPN logins that use a configuration or key from an old mailbox or leak), cloud control-plane audit (administration commands issued to many instances through the cloud systems manager, instance metadata queries from an application), process lineage (a legitimate GameHook binary renamed svchost.exe loading a malicious DLL) and endpoint inventory queries for hosts without the security agent; CrowdStrike lists ARTEX-named command-line parameters, cloud roles and a directory under ProgramData as hunt markers (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).
Defender takeaway
Rotate keys held in old directory exports and backups, require signed SAML assertions and IMDSv2, and hunt authentication and cloud audit logs for the parallel, many-target pattern an operator-steered agent produces; CrowdStrike expects China-nexus actors to keep adopting agent frameworks (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).

item.title: Talos IR Q3: public administration tied for most targeted; vishing into RMM and EDR killing mark the ransomware cases
item.description: Cisco Talos Incident Response's Q3 2026 trends report names public administration, tied with finance at 18 percent of engagements, as the most targeted sector, and puts phishing first and public-facing application exploitation second among initial-access techniques. Its ransomware cases (27 percent of engagements) show help-desk vishing that leads the victim to allow remote access through a legitimate remote-management tool, and operators who uninstall or terminate EDR, including with vulnerable drivers.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOB2

ANNUAL REPORT: Cisco Talos Incident Response trends Q3 2026: public administration tied with finance as the most targeted sector, help-desk vishing into remote-management tools, and ransomware operators uninstalling and killing EDR

Cisco Talos Incident Response reports that in Q3 2026 financial organisations made up 18 percent of its engagements, tying with public administration as the most targeted sector (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Phishing was the leading initial-access technique at 37 percent of engagements and exploitation of public-facing applications second at 33 percent; the phishing cases include numerous actors who phone the victim as the IT help desk to get remote access allowed through a legitimate remote monitoring and management (RMM) tool (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Ransomware and pre-ransomware cases were 27 percent of engagements, with The Gentlemen, Qilin, Rhysida and the closed group Interlock among the families and a new variant, VYPR, that Talos calls operationally immature: it had no leak site when seen, reused leaked Conti-derived source code and exfiltrated over several days (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29).

The VYPR intrusion began with a vishing call that had the user start a Microsoft Quick Assist session; the actor then used RMM software that ran PowerShell to download and install an MSI from a remote address, with MeshAgent, Rclone, PsExec, an IP scanner and mstsc as tools, and disabled EDR with several vulnerable drivers (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Interlock operators repeatedly tried to uninstall Cisco Secure Endpoint, used PsExec and taskkill to end security services and integrity checkers, turned off Windows Defender real-time protection and cleared event logs (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Talos names insufficient logging (over 40 percent of engagements), weak credential and secret handling, and absent or incomplete MFA as the most common weaknesses, and recommends centralised logging with at least 90 days of retention (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
An organisation whose help desk or staff can be reached by phone and whose endpoints permit Quick Assist or an unapproved RMM agent; Talos names public administration among the most targeted sectors in its caseload.
Detection
In process-creation and software-install telemetry, an RMM or Quick Assist session started after an inbound call, followed by PowerShell run under the RMM agent that downloads an installer from an external address; in endpoint and service-control telemetry, attempts to uninstall the EDR agent, PsExec or taskkill ending security services, Defender real-time protection switched off, vulnerable kernel drivers loaded, and event logs cleared.
Defender takeaway
Treat a remote-support session that nobody at the help desk started as the vishing signal and inventory which RMM tools and Quick Assist are permitted on endpoints; alert on EDR uninstall and security-service termination as a ransomware precursor; and centralise logs with the 90-day minimum retention Talos recommends, because actors delete logs on the endpoint.

item.title: Machelen municipality: foothold from a website's misleading instructions, 22 days to detection; Rhysida lists its files
item.description: The Belgian municipality of Machelen published a timeline in which attackers gained access to an internal laptop through misleading instructions on an external website on 2026-08-20, reached a user with high privileges on 2026-09-10 and were found on 2026-09-11; it confirms that personal data was stolen. Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-10-27 that the Rhysida group had listed the municipal and social-welfare file servers on its leak site, a claim the municipality has not confirmed.
item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOA2

Machelen (Belgium) municipality: its own timeline shows a foothold through misleading instructions on an external website on 2026-08-20, found 22 days later after a high-privilege user was reached, with personal data confirmed stolen and Rhysida now listing municipal and social-welfare files

Machelen's own timeline records that on 2026-08-20 attackers gained access to an internal laptop through misleading instructions on an external website, explored it extensively from 24 August to 1 September, and on 10 September had access to a user with high access rights and other IT systems; the municipality found the incident on 11 September, isolated all systems, reported to the Belgian CCB-CERT, restarted part of its systems from a backup of a safe date on 14 September and recorded the first evidence of leaked data on 17 September (Municipality of Machelen, 2026-09-22). It confirms that personal data was leaked and says the scope is still being investigated (Municipality of Machelen, 2026-09-22); the mayor had said on 14 September that no personal data appeared to be affected, and ITdaily reports that this proved wrong (ITdaily, 2026-09-23). Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-10-27 that Rhysida listed Machelen on its leak site, describing the listing as municipal and social-welfare file servers of about 1.3 million files, with client files that include passports and identity cards, nursing-home medical files and civil-status records, which are the group's own claims (Ransomware.live, 2026-10-27).

Detection
The timeline puts 22 days between first access and detection, with the first laptop explored from 24 August to 1 September; it names neither the website nor the commands, so the telemetry to review includes endpoint process creation after a user followed instructions on a web page and later use of a high-privilege account from that workstation, which is an inference from the timeline.
Defender takeaway
Treat a user who followed instructions from a website on a work laptop as a possible intrusion that can sit unseen for weeks; review high-privilege account activity from the user's workstation for the weeks after the event, not only the day it is reported.

item.title: Moldova: unauthenticated e-government services queried for about one million ID numbers; data on 750,000 extracted
item.description: Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency says that between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-23 attackers exploited flaws in state digital services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and, on preliminary estimates, extract data sets for about 750,000 of them, then used what they obtained to extract more from interconnected systems. The Prime Minister says foreign state involvement is being investigated and that AI allegedly helped find the flaws; Moldova has not attributed the attack, and the agency took 82 services under review and disconnected exposed services and more than 30 systems.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOA2

Moldova's government digital services: attackers used flaws in services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and extract data on about 750,000 of them between 19 and 23 October, and the Prime Minister says AI allegedly helped find the flaws

Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency (AGE) reported on 2026-10-27 that between 19 and 23 October attackers queried about one million national identification numbers (IDNPs) through state digital services and that, on preliminary estimates, data sets for about 750,000 of them were extracted; MOLDPRES had put the access requests at about 11 million on 2026-10-24 (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27; MOLDPRES, 2026-10-24). AGE's technical explanation is that the attackers exploited vulnerabilities in services reachable without authentication and then used the data they obtained for further extractions; the first attacks hit an electronic service that logged the legal basis of processing incorrectly, which is why citizens saw entries for civil-status document requests and driving-licence issue in the data-access history of the EVO app (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27). Data that may be affected, not every category for every person, includes name, date and place of birth, first-degree relatives, insured status, family doctor, social benefits, pensions, disability, driving licence, photograph, vehicles and companies owned or run, IBAN, tax debts and payment history; AGE says card data is not held on the platform and it found no unauthorised change to state registers (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27).

AGE stopped the extraction on 23 October at 11:30, reviewed 82 digital services and suspended the exposed ones, and its timeline says 82 public services and more than 30 information systems and administration panels were disconnected as a precaution on 23 October; it blocked further attempts on 25 and 27 October, and the Prime Minister's account is that 30 of the 82 services were disconnected (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27; MOLDPRES, 2026-10-28). The Prime Minister says the incident is not isolated, that foreign state actors are being investigated and that the attackers automated the extraction, with the use of artificial intelligence allegedly facilitating the identification and exploitation of the vulnerabilities (MOLDPRES, 2026-10-28). Moldova has not attributed the attack to any country or group (The Record, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
A public e-service of a federal, cantonal or communal administration that returns person data for an identifier without authentication, or whose output feeds other registers, since AGE says the extraction chained from unauthenticated services into further data (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27).
Detection
Citizens noticed the abuse because the data-access history in the EVO app showed processing for civil-status document requests and driving-licence issue that they had not made, so a data-subject-visible access log is a detection channel (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27). On the server side the relevant telemetry is per-service request volume and sequential or bulk identifier lookups from one source; the sources give no breakdown of the request pattern, so that is an inference from about 11 million requests against about one million numbers.
Defender takeaway
List the public services that answer for a person identifier without authentication and check what each one returns, whether it feeds other registers and whether its access log records the true purpose; rate limits and alerts on bulk lookups belong in front of every such service.

item.description: SafePay claimed an attack on the Bernese wastewater-treatment association ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal on 2026-09-15, and Inside IT reports of 2026-10-27 that the group has now put about 49 GB of stolen data into the darknet. item.content:encoded:
ROUTINENATOC3

ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal (canton Bern, communal wastewater-treatment association): SafePay has put about 49 GB into the darknet, which Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT, finds holds personal records, bank statements, weak passwords and a third party's monitoring credentials; the association declines to comment

The tracker DeXpose recorded on 2026-09-15 that SafePay had claimed an attack on ARA Lyss, the wastewater-treatment association at ara-lyss.ch, posting that the full leak would be published soon unless a company representative made contact (DeXpose, 2026-09-15). Inside IT reported on 2026-10-27 that SafePay has put the stolen data into the darknet, about 49 GB in the case of the Bernese association ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal, that the security firm Risikomonitor analysed it, and that the association's management declined to comment (Inside IT, 2026-10-27). Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT and not verified independently, finds about 3,200 e-mail addresses and data on more than 1,200 identifiable persons; user folders and a data store with content up to March 2026 that hold 255 password hits, 195 of them very weak; bank statements and a transaction list with more than 100 payments by private persons with name and address; the full login data to the monitoring portals of the photovoltaic plants of another company's customers, stored on the same server; and a 2015 applicant list with birth dates, civil status, former employer and interview notes that was never deleted (Inside IT, 2026-10-27).

BACS told Inside IT that SafePay, which relies on double extortion, is among the more active ransomware groups in Switzerland and, together with The Gentlemen, the third most active in 2026 after Akira and Payload, that it has no clear focus on Switzerland, and that it was first observed there in May 2025 (Inside IT, 2026-10-27). No source says how the attackers got in or that data was encrypted at the association.

Defender takeaway
A communal body or association should look for credentials, bank statements and applicant files on its own file servers before an attacker does: Risikomonitor found 255 password hits in files, another company's portal logins and a 2015 applicant list that had never been deleted, and those are what a published dump gives fraudsters (Inside IT, 2026-10-27).

item.description: Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27, fixing two unauthenticated read-side SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 (the sort-by parameter of store and category post lists) and CVE-2026-102789 (an editor task without a permission check), both scored CVSS 4.0 9.3 by the Joomla CNA and affecting every release up to 2.20.4.1. No exploitation is reported, Joomla 3 sites have no fix, and the action now points at 2.20.4.2.
item.content:encoded:
Update28 Oct 2026 03:52 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelactionsbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27, fixing two unauthenticated read-side SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 (the sort-by parameter of store and category post lists) and CVE-2026-102789 (an editor task without a permission check), both scored CVSS 4.0 9.3 by the Joomla CNA and affecting every release up to 2.20.4.1. No exploitation is reported, Joomla 3 sites have no fix, and the action now points at 2.20.4.2.

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27 with two security fixes rated Critical, for the versions 2.20.4.1 and earlier (Balbooa, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-102788 is in the sort-by URL parameter of store and category post lists and CVE-2026-102789 is a missing permission check on the editor task that loads blog posts (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27); Balbooa's fixes are a strict allowlist validation for the sort-by parameter and a user edit-level check on the editor task (Balbooa, 2026-10-27). mySites.guru says the sort value previously went into the ORDER BY part of the database query and reads the second flaw as a second anonymous route to the same query. mySites.guru reports that the Joomla CNA scores both CVSS 4.0 9.3 and lists every release from 1.0.0 to 2.20.4.1 as affected, and that only two PHP files differ between 2.20.4.1 and 2.20.4.2, one per fix (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27).

mySites.guru reads both flaws as read-side, although the CNA's vector also rates integrity and availability High: an anonymous visitor can extract the Joomla user table, with its password hashes, and every other table the site's extensions created. mySites.guru says about 95% of the Gridbox sites it monitors ran an affected version on the morning of the release, that sites on the Joomla 3 line stop at Gridbox 2.17.0.2, which has no fix for this year's flaws, and that there is no public report of exploitation yet (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27). Nothing here is reported exploited, unlike the July batches above; the version to be on is now 2.20.4.2.

Detection
In web access and database query logs, store or category list requests whose sort-by value is not one of the known sort keys, repeated anonymous calls to the Gridbox editor's blog-post task, and slow-query bursts from the web account; since the reported impact is data read out, the post-patch check is credential hygiene on a site that was exposed, starting with administrator accounts nobody created, since the password hashes can be worked on offline.
Defender takeaway
Update to 2.20.4.2 now, communal and agency sites included, and move Joomla 3 sites to a supported Joomla (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27).

Open finding: CVE-2026-61425 and the follow-up batch, Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: a client-supplied cookie is accepted as proof of identity, giving anonymous Super User access →

item.content:encoded:
Update27 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

Seoul police referred the leader of a criminal group to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for stealing 8.2 million records from more than 90 organizations, hospitals and universities among them, and extorting 38; BleepingComputer reports that the group used ARTEX, so the framework is now documented in criminal extortion use as well as in Storm-0940's state-aligned activity.

Seoul Metropolitan Police announced on 2026-10-26 that it referred a 32-year-old gang leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23, with six accomplices investigated without detention, for taking 8.2 million personal-data records and internal files from more than 90 organizations since September 2025, among them cram schools, hospitals, golf courses, universities and large-company affiliates, and for sending extortion e-mails (Yonhap, 2026-10-26, translated from Korean). BleepingComputer, citing local media, reports that the group demanded 360 million won (about USD 270,000) in 38 of the incidents in exchange for not leaking the data, that the police say the leader used the ARTEX framework, the same system used in the attacks on South Korean banks, and that he moved from conventional tools to AI utilities in late August 2026 (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26). Yonhap counts 60 of the victims as hacked with AI and describes the system as the AI autonomous penetration-testing system used in the recent financial-sector data thefts without naming it, so the ARTEX name is BleepingComputer's (Yonhap, 2026-10-26). No encryption step is reported, and the police say AI lowered the barrier to entry and call this the first arrest in Korea in a large-scale hacking and personal-data theft case that exploited generative AI (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26). The framework is therefore in use by a financially motivated criminal group as well as by the state-aligned actor Microsoft describes; no source reports a Swiss victim.

Open finding: ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration →
